chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Saif ibn 'Umayra, from Abu al-Subah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding the weakened who do not find a way out nor are guided to a path: They are unable to use a stratagem to enter into disbelief, nor are they guided to enter into faith; thus, they are of no consequence with regards to disbelief and faith.

key_terms.الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ: The weakened or those lacking power/means

ai.seo_question: What is the theological status of those who are too weak to choose between faith and disbelief?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s ruling on the *mustad'afin* (the weak), clarifying that their inability to exert effort (*jahd*) in either embracing Islam or accepting disbelief exempts them from the full accountability of the binary categories. This highlights the Shia principle of *taklif* (obligation) being proportional to one's capacity and circumstances, distinguishing passive incapacity from active rejection. The narration underscores that divine judgment considers the internal state and capability of the individual rather than merely their external affiliation.
